teacher_info.about_teacher:
I graduated from university in Chile, where I studied to become a teacher of English. While still a student I won a scholarship to live in England and work as a Spanish tutor in a language school, so that experience really helped me become more fluent and relaxed about my use of English. I discovered that the most important thing when learning a language isn't to speak perfectly or with a specific accent, but to actually be able to communicate with other people and be understood, that's when learning really becomes motivating. 
In 2017 I took the CELTA course which gave me a different perspective on how to teach using ONLY English, something I thought almost impossible.
teacher_info.teaching_style:
My lessons are based on conversation, so it all depends on the topics that interest you the most. I will also use short video clips or images to encourage communication. These materials all have some grammar point or new expression or vocabulary, so you won't end the class feeling like you haven't learnt anything. On the first lesson I will ask you some questions to get to know each other a bit and so I can see what level you have. I will suggest a topic for the lesson and from there on we will agree together what's the next step :) 
We can also follow a coursebook if you'd like to have a structured pace. I like to work with motivated students who are willing to put some effort :)

If you do it after, I'm sorry but italki will charge you for the lesson and my time. If you have any questions please ask italki's support for advice.

Presentations: Skills for presenting legal arguments effectively.

Courtroom Skills: Practice for speaking in court, including direct examination and cross-examination.

4. Reading Comprehension
Case Law Analysis: Techniques for reading and interpreting case law and legal opinions.
Statutory Interpretation: Understanding how to read and analyze statutes and regulations.

5. Practical Applications
Mock Trials: Participate in simulated trials to apply your skills in a real-world context.
Role-Playing Exercises: Engage in role-playing scenarios to practice negotiation and client interaction.

6. Cultural Aspects of Law
Legal Systems: Overview of different legal systems (common law vs. civil law) and their terminology.
